newsitem.title: UK: UK's Labour backs Blair's manifesto by huge margin.
newsitem.headline: UK's Labour backs Blair's manifesto by huge margin.

text.p: Tony Blair's grip on the UK's main opposition Labour party was underscored on Friday when its annual conference voted overwhelmingly to endorse the party's pre-election manifesto.
The margin of victory was 94.64 percent to 5.36 percent. The result of the vote, taken on Thursday, was announced at the start of the final day of the conference.
The document, "New Labour new life for Britain" will now be put to a postal ballot of all Labour's 400,000 members, further locking the party into Blair's modernising agenda.

The document is based on Labour's five core election pledges -- smaller class sizes, fast-track justice for persistent young offenders, cutting NHS waiting lists, getting 250,000 under-25s off welfare and into work, and observing sound economic policies.

Constituency delegates, which have half the votes at conference, voted for the document by 45.26 percent to 4.74 percent. Affiliated organisations, mainly trade unions, backed it by 49.38 percent to 0.62 percent.
